subject: Post-call: Bancorp discovery — reliability expectations & graceful degradation plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bancorp.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@bancorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Bancorp discovery — reliability expectations & graceful degradation plan

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we loop in your infra/security teams. I kept this tight — tell me if anything is off.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: user-facing hallucinations and periodic latency spikes for internal policy-generation workflows; outages during heavy batch runs (monthly reporting) have resulted in degraded downstream systems.
- Impact: 3 incidents in past 6 months (two partial, one >30m outage) — current runbook requires manual failover and takes 45–90 minutes to restore full service.
- Goals: 99.9% availability for synchronous endpoints (policy gen), 95th p50 latency targets <800ms for interactive flows, predictable cost under peak.

Current stack (from your notes)
- Primary: in-house microservice that calls an external LLM vendor with per-request throttling
- On-prem batch workers for scheduled reports
- No prefix caching; KV-cache not currently used

Reliability & graceful degradation notes we discussed
- Incident history: you confirmed three incidents around capacity/backpressure and one occasion of region-level cloud disruption (fraud detection window was impacted).
- Fallback appetite: you are open to multi-region active/passive routing and using a smaller, cheaper local model for degraded responses rather than blocking.
- Success criteria you gave: automated fallback that keeps app responsive (responses can be shorter / lower fidelity but must not hallucinate on account IDs), and a post-incident RCA within 24 hours.

Proposed initial plan (what Redwood would deliver in PoC)
1) Baseline measurement run — capture p50/p95 latencies, token costs, and failure modes for 72 hours.
2) Prefix/KV cache enabled for hottest prompts; validate latency improvement on read-heavy flows.
3) Graceful-degradation policy: primary large model in region A + staged fallback to a quantized regional replica or a smaller model in region B; safe-mode output filter to suppress hallucinated sensitive fields.
4) SLO proposal: 99.9% availability with automatic fallback; 95th p50 latency target adjustments after baseline.

Action items / next steps
- From Bancorp: send incident postmortems for the three incidents (attachments okay) and a list of the top 10 production prompts we should prioritize for caching/filtering (due: Mar 13).
- From Redwood (me, Neha): share PoC scope & estimate and SLO template (attached). I’ll also put Jordan (solutions) and Vivek (reliability lead) on the thread for a short technical sync.
- Technical sync: propose Thu Mar 12, 10:00–11:00 PT — 30–45m focused call to align on infra/egress/VPC needs.

Risks we flagged
- Legal/security constraints around exporting tokens to external regions — may need Private deployment or VPC egress controls.
- Some prompts contain PII/sensitive account identifiers — will require redaction or strict KMS/HSM controls.

Attachments: bancorp-initial-map.pdf (one-page mutual action plan), slo-draft-templates.xlsx (sample SLO matrix).

If this matches, I’ll follow up with the PoC writeup and calendar invites.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

—
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bancorp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Bancorp Security <security@bancorp.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Bancorp discovery — reliability expectations & graceful degradation plan

Neha —

Thanks for the clean recap. This is largely accurate. A couple of clarifications:
- The two partial incidents were throttling-related during ETL peaks; the full outage was due to a regional vendor incident and our fallback didn’t trigger automatically.
- We do have a short incident summary for each event; I’ll put those in a single PDF and share by EOD Wed (Mar 11).
- Security: our compliance group will need the PoC network diagram and a summary of any data leaving our VPC — expect security@bancorp.com to request more detail.

We’re comfortable with a degraded-mode response that is shorter/flagged as “best-effort” as long as account IDs and transaction values are never hallucinated. Is there an agreed approach you recommend for output redaction vs. deterministic masking?

Tech sync on Thu Mar 12 10:00 PT works for Sam and me — please send an invite.

Best,
Alex
Sr. Product Manager, Policy Automation
Alex.Rivera@bancorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@bancorp.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@bancorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Bancorp discovery — reliability expectations & graceful degradation plan

Alex / Sam —

Quick answer on redaction vs. masking from the engineering side:
- For PoC we recommend a two-layer approach: 1) deterministic masking for account IDs (hash + prefix) to preserve linkage without exposing raw values; 2) output filtering rules for numeric fields (transaction amounts) where values above a threshold return a token like "[REDACTED_AMT]" with an accompanying confidence score.
- If masking breaks analytic correlation for you, we can run a hybrid where the masked ID is reversible inside your VPC only (via a customer KMS) — that requires a private deployment or egress controls we’ll detail in the diagram.

I’ll attach a short tech sketch (internal) to the meeting invite and bring a reliability engineer. Looking forward to Thursday.

—
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
